task.title: Resolve Conflicts with AI
task.shortdesc: Let analyze a conflict and propose a resolution you can review and apply.

step.cmd: Right-click the conflicting file and select .

info.note: This action works on text files only, so it is not offered for image or SVG conflicts. If the file is too large for the AI context window, the operation stops with an error rather than sending only part of the file.

step.stepresult: analyzes the conflicting file and its common ancestor, then opens the window.

info.p: The pane explains, in plain language, what each side changed. Four comparison views let you inspect the proposal (Resolved vs Mine, Resolved vs Theirs, Resolved vs Conflicted, and Mine vs Theirs) where Mine is your version, Theirs is the incoming change, and Resolved is the AI proposal (always shown on the left). The resolved file is editable in each view, allowing you to fine-tune it (use Restore original AI suggestion to undo your edits).
info.note: During a rebase, these labels follow Git's own convention, which is the reverse of a merge: Mine is the branch you are rebasing onto (the new base), and Theirs is the commit being replayed (your own work). The AI explanation and the comparison views use this same orientation.

result.p: The Git Client writes the resolution to your working copy and stages the file.
